podcast.body: This album won the Grammy for Album of the Year in early 1985. Its title inspired the name of Michael Angelo Matos's book, "Can't Slow Down: How 1984 Became Pop's Blockbuster Year," which delves into the pop cultural phenomena of 1984. "named after the Lionel Richie album Cancelo Down that won the Grammy for album of the year in early 1985."

podcast.body: This album, described as a "Yuppie Soul Blockbuster," won Album of the Year at the 1985 Grammy Awards, despite strong competition from albums like Prince's "Purple Rain" and Bruce Springsteen's "Born in the U.S.A." It was a commercial "smash," equaling or exceeding the sales of its fellow nominees and generating many "culture-blanketing hits." Richie's music was seen by the Academy's elders as the "kind of smooth shaman they found legible." "Lionel Richie's Yuppie Soul Blockbuster can't slow down."

podcast.body: This album, released by Lionel Richie, who turned 35 in 1984, became his biggest and most hit-packed LP ever. It produced an impressive five top ten hits, including two number ones, and contributed to his status as a veteran soloist scoring major successes in 1984. "Lionel Richey, whose can't slow down LP produced five top ten hits, including two number ones."
